# Results — Study 102 (Free-Rebalance) on the real multi-asset total-return tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — a fixed-weight
**50/50 SPY/TLT** portfolio, **rebalanced** back to target (annual and quarterly, charging
**10 bps one-way per rebalance**) vs the same initial weights left to **drift**
(buy-and-hold), on **total-return** tapes over the honest common window (**TLT starts
2002-07**). The headline "free lunch" number is the **realised rebalancing bonus** =
rebalanced CAGR − drift CAGR. We also report the textbook **Booth-Fama / Willenbrock
diversification-return identity** (the source of the myth), a **block-bootstrap CI** on the
daily bonus, and the bonus **by sub-period**. As-of **2026-06-12**; match the fingerprints
to confirm you hold the same tape.*

> SPY trades from 1993 but **TLT from 2002-07** and GLD from 2004-11, so the aligned
> 50/50 SPY/TLT window honestly starts 2002-07-30 — never back-filled.

## The honest test — net of 10 bps one-way per rebalance

| Arm | CAGR | Vol | Sharpe | Max drawdown | Rebalances |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Rebalanced (annual)** | 8.22% | **9.6%** | 0.875 | −28.9% | 25 |
| **Rebalanced (quarterly)** | 8.22% | 9.7% | 0.861 | −29.0% | 96 |
| Drift (buy & hold) | **8.82%** | 10.3% | 0.874 | **−26.9%** | 0 |

## The decisive numbers

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Realised rebalancing bonus (annual) | **−0.59 pts/yr** CAGR |
| Realised rebalancing bonus (quarterly) | **−0.60 pts/yr** CAGR |
| Sharpe: rebalanced (annual) vs drift | **0.875 vs 0.874** (a wash) |
| Booth-Fama diversification return (vs weighted-avg of constituents) | **+0.90 pts/yr** (var reduction 1.81 pts) |
| HAC *t* on the daily bonus (annual reb − drift) | **−1.19** |
| Block-bootstrap 95% CI on the daily bonus | **[−0.660, +0.132] bps/day** (straddles 0) |
| Bonus, 2002–2013 sub-period | **+1.27 pts/yr** |
| Bonus, 2014–2026 sub-period | **−1.74 pts/yr** |
| Vol reduction vs drift (annual) | **−0.7 pts** (9.6% vs 10.3%) |

## How to read it

- **The "free lunch" did not pay.** Over the full 2002–2026 window the 50/50 SPY/TLT
  portfolio **rebalanced** earned **−0.59 pts/yr *less*** than the same weights left to
  drift (8.22% vs 8.82% CAGR), and the risk-adjusted return was a dead heat (Sharpe 0.875
  vs 0.874). Rebalancing was **not** a guaranteed bonus on this tape. → Signal **WEAK**,
  Tradability **MIRAGE** for the "adds return / free lunch" claim.
- **The textbook identity is real — but it answers a different question.** The Booth-Fama
  diversification return is **+0.90 pts/yr** and **always ≥ 0 by construction** — but its
  baseline is the *weighted average of the constituents*, **not** the drift portfolio. A
  drift portfolio also diversifies *and* lets the winner run, so it can (and here does)
  beat the rebalancer. Quoting the +0.90 as "the bonus you'd capture vs holding the
  basket" is the sleight of hand that turns a variance identity into a free lunch.
- **The bonus is regime-dependent and can flip sign.** It was **+1.27 pts/yr** in
  2002–2013 (a choppy, mean-reverting decade where harvesting paid) and **−1.74 pts/yr**
  in 2014–2026 (stocks ran away from bonds, so trimming the winner cost you). The
  block-bootstrap CI on the daily bonus **straddles zero** and HAC *t* = −1.19 — the sign
  is not statistically distinguishable from noise on the full sample.
- **What rebalancing *does* deliver is risk control.** Volatility falls **9.6% vs 10.3%**
  and the weights stay pinned at the target risk mix instead of drifting to a
  stock-heavy book. (Max drawdown is a touch *worse* — −28.9% vs −26.9% — precisely
  because the un-rebalanced book drifted toward more equity during the bull run; the
  point is rebalancing *controls the mix*, not that it always cuts the worst loss.)
  → 3rd axis **CONFIRMED** (controls risk), on the volatility/weight-discipline read.

## Spine (offline sign controls, `run_synthetic_demo.py`)

| Tape | Expected bonus | Realised bonus (quarterly) | Sign |
|---|---|--:|---|
| Mean-reverting equal-drift pair (Shannon's Demon) | **positive** | **+0.77 pts/yr** | OK |
| One asset persistently trends | **negative** | **−3.90 pts/yr** | OK |

The harness banks a **positive** bonus when assets mean-revert around equal drift and a
**negative** bonus when one asset trends — it measures the *sign* correctly, so the
negative real-tape reading is a finding, not a bug.

## Reproduce

```bash
python examples/verify.py              # real tape (this doc)
python examples/run_synthetic_demo.py  # offline positive/negative sign controls
```
